preflight.py:224-226 comment claims SQLite mode=rw silently falls back to read-only on a 0444 file. SQLite's sqlite3_open_v2 docs for SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE: 'opened for reading and writing if possible, or reading only if the file is write protected by the operating system'; URI mode=rw maps to that flag (only mode=rw avoids create, not read-only fallback). Falsifying input (0444 file where mode=rw raises) does not occur: open succeeds read-only and errors only at write time. The code at 227-230 uses open(r+b) instead, which raises PermissionError on 0444, consistent with the comment. Not run empirically; based on documented semantics.

preflight.py:197-199 docstring matches code: probe_memory opens chroma.sqlite3 with open(store_file,'r+b') and closes it (229-230). POSIX fcntl advisory locks are per-process/inode, so closing any fd on the file releases all the process's locks on it; SQLite's default unix VFS uses fcntl locks and documents this caveat (File Locking and Concurrency / 'How To Corrupt'). Absolute-claim trace: process holds a SQLite connection (default VFS) then opens/closes a second fd on the same file -> locks dropped, which is why the probe must precede opening the store. A non-default VFS (unix-flock, OFD) would not drop locks, but Chroma uses the default VFS and the docstring is scoped to 'on unix' for this store; no such VFS is selected in the repo, so the counterexample is not reachable by a shipped caller.

preflight.py:229-230 opens store_file with mode 'r+b' and a bare `pass`: r+b neither truncates nor creates (missing file raises FileNotFoundError, handled by return at 231-232), and no write/flush/seek occurs on the handle, so contents and size are unchanged. Hostile input considered: existing 0444 or read-only file raises PermissionError -> PreflightError, still no modification. The sentinel file is in the directory, not the store, and is unlinked. Function docstring (190-191) agrees ('nothing written').

preflight.py:228-239: open(store_file,'r+b') in try; FileNotFoundError -> return (line 231-232, caught before generic OSError); except OSError: PermissionError (EACCES/EPERM) or errno==EROFS (plain OSError in Python) -> 'memory store file ... is not writable by this process'; else (IsADirectoryError, ELOOP, ENOTDIR) -> 'cannot open memory store file ... for writing'; both raise PreflightError('memory', detail) from exc. errno imported at line 26. Matches Python's errno mapping.

The claim's description matches the code. tests/unit/test_preflight.py:342-353 makes chroma.sqlite3 a directory and asserts 'cannot open memory store file' and no 'not writable by this process' and no PermissionError cause. It has no platform skip; the only skipif in scope is _skip_when_root at 320-323. probe_memory (src/sqllens/preflight.py:229-238) opens with 'r+b' and routes any PermissionError or EROFS to the 'not writable by this process' text. On POSIX, opening a directory raises IsADirectoryError, which is not a PermissionError, so the test passes there. On Windows, opening a directory raises PermissionError (this is Python/OS behaviour I did not run), so the negative assertions would fail there. However, the repo's ci.yml jobs all run on ubuntu-latest, and only mcpb.yml uses a windows-latest matrix, for building the package. I found no shipped caller or repository requirement that runs this unit test on Windows, so no requirement is shown broken. I cannot tell whether Windows unit-test runs are required, so I cannot grade this as FAIL or INVALID. Not run: the unit suite on Windows.
